text: Condrox AI is a cognitive conversational intelligence platform built by Tobias Østen in Norway. It is a hybrid AI system that understands language without using large language models (LLMs). Condrox AI uses an 18-stage cognitive pipeline, 26 conversational intelligence components, and 5 mode agents to process requests. The current version is 3.4.0 with 938 passing tests. It is a pre-release system demonstrating that non-LLM AI can produce coherent, context-aware responses.

Condrox AI differs from LLMs because it does not use neural networks or transformer architectures. Instead, it uses symbolic reasoning, deterministic algorithms, and a knowledge backend with BM25 similarity search. LLMs generate text by predicting the next token; Condrox AI processes input through a structured pipeline of 18 stages, each with a specific algorithmic purpose. This makes Condrox AI deterministic, debuggable, and transparent — you can trace exactly why a response was produced.

The 18-stage cognitive pipeline is the core of Condrox AI. Each stage is a callable function that transforms a BrainState object. The stages are: 01 input validation, 02 intent classification, 03 mode selection, 04 domain routing, 05 context building, 06 knowledge fetch, 07 memory integration, 08 reasoning core, 08b agent execution, 09 synthesis, 09b quality guardrail, 10 output stabilization, 11 language enforcement, 12 response styling, 13 delivery, 14 safety check, 15 ethics check, 16 metadata. The pipeline is a fold/reduce over these ordered stages.

Condrox AI has 5 mode agents: Default Agent for general conversation, Code Agent for programming tasks, Explain Agent for explanations, Analyze Agent for analysis, and Architect Agent for system design. The mode selector at stage 03 chooses which agent to activate based on the classified intent. Each agent produces a draft response that is then refined by the synthesis and quality stages.

Condrox AI has 26 conversational intelligence components organized in 6 groups: Phase 2-A Critical Stabilization (4 components), Phase 2-B Conversational Quality (5 components), Phase 2-C Observability and Safety (3 components), Phase 2-D Agent Coordination (3 components), Phase 2-E Advanced Conversational Intelligence (7 components), and Phase 2-F System-Level Properties (4 components). All 26 components are active with zero dead code.

Condrox AI has a knowledge backend with 21,917 knowledge items across 15 domains including language, grammar, semantics, dialog, social intelligence, ethics, values, morality, reasoning, logic, culture, common sense, cognitive models, world knowledge, and school curriculum. The knowledge backend uses BM25 similarity search with TF-IDF scoring for retrieval. A knowledge graph provides expanded retrieval through Jaccard similarity edges between items.

Condrox AI was built by one person, Tobias Østen, in Norway over 8 months of focused work. The codebase is approximately 25,000 lines of code (SLOC). The replacement cost estimated using COCOMO II is approximately 4.7 million USD. The system has 938 passing tests covering unit, integration, API, storage, admin API, and AI-OS components.

Condrox AI uses a Word Identity System with approximately 185 words across 5 modular JSON stores: social words (greetings, question words, politeness), emotion words (with emotion labels), programming words (code, algorithms, data structures), architecture words (design, analysis, trade-offs), and AI words (AI/ML concepts, science, explain actions). The Word Identity Engine provides O(1) lookup and softmax intent classification.

Condrox AI has a creative stack that maps detected emotions to music generation parameters. The EmotionDetector identifies 10 emotion labels: neutral, happy, sad, angry, anxious, grateful, confused, curious, philosophical, and personal. The EmotionPaletteMapper converts emotions to musical parameters including genre, tempo (BPM), key, energy, and valence. The MusicPromptBuilder generates text prompts for music generation models.

Condrox AI has an AI Operating System (AI-OS) with 8 subsystems: EventBus for pub/sub messaging with 8 event types, ServiceManager for lifecycle management with topological sorting, BootManager for 6 staged boot phases, MonitorLoop for background health monitoring, StateManager for SQLite checkpoint and recovery, TaskQueue for priority task scheduling, SelfRepairManager with circuit breakers, and AIOSKernel as the central orchestrator.

Condrox AI has a security layer that checks both input and output. Input security detects prompt injection, malicious patterns, and blocked topics. Output security detects PII leakage (email, phone, credit card numbers), secret leakage, and prompt injection echoes. The ethics engine checks content against policy rules. Safety checks run on both input before the pipeline and output after the pipeline.

Condrox AI has a quality guardrail that gates every response before delivery. The quality gate evaluates output on multiple dimensions including coherence, relevance, safety, and completeness. Responses that fail the quality gate are blocked or rewritten. The quality score ranges from 0.0 to 1.0. Conversational intents like greet, clarify, and emotional bypass the quality guardrail to preserve legitimate content.

Condrox AI has a memory system with semantic memory storage. The MemoryManager stores conversation items with tags for multi-turn recall. A MemoryStabilizationLayer runs before each request to consolidate memory. A ConversationalMemoryGraph tracks relationships between memory items. Memory can be persisted to SQLite via the StorageBackend. The PreReleaseAgent disables memory writes to ensure zero cross-user contamination.

Condrox AI has a reasoning core at stage 08 that combines domain knowledge, memory, and evidence to produce reasoning facts. The reasoning core uses a claim ranker to prioritize evidence. The synthesis stage 09 combines reasoning facts, agent drafts, and knowledge into a final response draft. The response style engine applies tone and formatting based on the intent.

Condrox AI has a REST API built with FastAPI. The main endpoints are /health for health checks, /process for pipeline processing, /process/stream for SSE streaming, /creative for music generation, /status for system status, /metrics for Prometheus metrics, and /auth/login for authentication. The API uses API key authentication, rate limiting with slowapi, and CORS configuration. The admin API has 24 endpoints for dashboard management.

Condrox AI is deployed using Docker with a multi-stage build and gunicorn. Kubernetes manifests include 9 manifests with Horizontal Pod Autoscaler scaling from 2 to 10 replicas. CI/CD runs through GitHub Actions with security scanning via Bandit and Trivy. Observability is provided by Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboards. The Docker container runs as a non-root user for security.

Condrox AI has a School System with curriculum-based learning. The school system ingests lessons as knowledge items with domain='school' so the pipeline can retrieve verified, structured answers for school queries. Each lesson has a title, concepts, explanation, examples, and context rules. The school curriculum covers multiple subjects and provides hallucination-free educational content.

Condrox AI has a PreReleaseAgent for public website demonstrations. The PreReleaseAgent provides isolated, no-authentication chat with zero cross-user contamination. It uses a dedicated BrainController instance, disables memory writes with store_memory=False, and caps input at 500 characters and output at 1000 characters. Sessions are ephemeral with a 30-minute TTL and last 5 turns of history. Rate limiting is 10 requests per minute per IP.

Condrox AI processes requests through the pipeline using a BrainState object. BrainState is immutable and uses with_field() to create updated copies. The state tracks request_id, raw_input, processed_input, intent, mode, domain, emotion, confidence, security_approved, ethical_approved, final_output, errors, and metadata. The pipeline is a fold/reduce over 18 stages, each transforming the state.

Condrox AI has a context manager that tracks conversation context across turns. The ContextManager stores key-value pairs including domain, mode, intent, topic, and conversation history. A DCL (Declarative Context Language) engine loads defaults and steps through context rules. The context is built at stage 05 and used by subsequent stages for knowledge fetch, reasoning, and synthesis.

Condrox AI has an intent classifier at stage 02 that uses the Word Identity Engine as the primary classifier. The engine classifies intents including question, greet, clarify, emotional, code, explain, analyze, architect, and default. Emotion detection uses word identity first, falling back to the EmotionDetector. Non-emotional intents like code, architect, analyze, and explain suppress spurious emotion detection.

Condrox AI has a domain router at stage 04 that routes requests to knowledge domains. The router uses keyword overlap between input tokens and domain keyword sets. Domains include programming, architecture, security, data, and general. For technical intents like code, architect, analyze, and explain, the router never allows routing to general domains. The KnowledgeRouterV2 provides enriched fallback domain suggestions.

Condrox AI has a knowledge fetch stage at stage 06 that retrieves relevant knowledge items using BM25 similarity search. The stage queries the knowledge backend with the selected domain and falls back to all domains if no results are found. For technical queries, the school domain is excluded from fallback results to prevent curriculum content from appearing in technical answers. The stage also queries the Wikidata API for real-time information.

Condrox AI has a synthesis stage at stage 09 that combines reasoning facts, agent drafts, and knowledge into a final response. The synthesis prioritizes conversational intents like greet and clarify before agent drafts. An output stabilizer normalizes the text. A language enforcer ensures correct language usage. A response style engine applies tone and formatting based on the intent and domain.

Condrox AI has a delivery stage at stage 13 that formats the final output for the user. The delivery stage applies metadata including the request ID, domain, mode, intent, and confidence. The final output is checked by the safety layer and quality guardrail before being returned. The BrainController returns the final BrainState with the final_output field containing the response text.

Condrox AI has a single-instance lock that prevents concurrent pipeline runs. The lock is configurable via BrainConfig.enable_single_instance_lock. When enabled, only one pipeline run can execute at a time. The PreReleaseAgent disables this lock so concurrent public requests do not block each other, since each request is isolated by session anyway.

Condrox AI has a SQLite persistence backend for memory and knowledge storage. The StorageBackend interface provides save and load methods. MemoryStore and KnowledgeBackend can persist their state to SQLite. The persistence path is configurable via BrainConfig.persistence_path. The PreReleaseAgent does not use persistence to ensure no data is stored between sessions.

Condrox AI has a heartbeat engine that monitors subsystem health. The engine registers health checks for memory, knowledge, and other subsystems. A health score is computed from the heartbeat results. The /health endpoint returns the aggregate health status. The /status endpoint returns full system status including all 26 conversational intelligence components.

Condrox AI has a priority engine that enqueues requests before pipeline processing. The priority engine manages a queue of pending requests and prioritizes them based on urgency. An agent arbiter coordinates agent execution. A search agent guard validates agent results. A token pressure regulator manages synthesis token usage. A latency compensation module adjusts delivery timing.

Condrox AI is a pre-release system. The current version is 3.4.0 with 938 passing tests. The system has 16 completed phases of development. It was built by Tobias Østen in Norway. The market value is estimated at 2.5 to 5.1 million USD with a most likely value of 3.7 million USD based on a blended valuation approach. The replacement cost using COCOMO II is approximately 4.7 million USD for 25,000 lines of code.
